answer: The umber is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the shale. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. What survives to the vault is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, weighted by independent path length, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
